openings.claim: Use bolted strip guides with pivoting retaining straps to capture nonworking plate margins mechanically; release the straps for gloved inspection.
openings.delta: Change the retention dependency from magnetic attraction or pad friction to opposing contact stops carried by the existing mounting slots. Drill strips only; form guides and accessible release tabs with pliers, using cork at contacts. Allocate four strips and the supplied bolts without modifying plate or carriage.
openings.prediction: Nearest rival: a magnet-assisted friction clamp. Its available magnetic holding differs between plates; geometric capture should retain either plate despite that difference. Expected distinguishing observation: the spare remains within 1 mm with engaged stops even if magnetic assistance is absent. This is a hypothesis, not demonstrated performance; weaker magnetic pull alone does not predict stroke slip.
openings.probe: First measure slots, plate margins and clearance with ruler; sketch opposing stops and the removal path. Proceed only if supplied strips can be formed and M4 bolts fit without carriage disassembly or forbidden modifications. Fabricate within eighty minutes. In twenty observation minutes, run one configuration three times for twenty strokes, with the spare in the final run. Mark position away from the working edge and measure displacement. Perform three timed removal/return checks, final check wearing supplied thick gloves. Handle nonworking margins only. Require every run within 1 mm and every check within sixty seconds; check returned position too. Observe stop contact, bolt loosening and clearance interference. These establish candidate fitness but do not alone exclude friction as its operating cause.
assumptions: Slot dimensions accept supplied bolts and support the required stop geometry.
Strip thickness permits plier forming and withstands unspecified stroke loads.
Accessible margins permit opposing stops, top restraint and gloved release wholly outside marked clearance.
Defeat conditions include guide flexure, inadequate slot travel, inaccessible fasteners, interference or failed displacement/time limits; resource caps require abandoning an unbuildable candidate.

assessment: One probe candidate; feasibility remains unresolved because mounting geometry, strip properties and stroke loads are unspecified. No constraint relaxation or deployment claim.
